cases.goal: Working Python developers who have never written a generator learn to stream large files.
cases.summary: A function with yield returns a generator. Each next() runs it to the next yield.

blocks.text: By the end of this module you can write a generator that reads a file one line at a time and predict what each next() call returns.

blocks.code:
def count_up(limit):
    n = 1
    while n <= limit:
        yield n
        n += 1

counter = count_up(3)
print(next(counter))
print(next(counter))
print(list(counter))
blocks.note: The first next() runs to the first yield and stops there. list() drains what is left.

blocks.title: The mistake everyone makes
blocks.text: Writing return n instead of yield n inside the loop. The function then hands back 1 and ends, so a loop over it sees a single number and never the rest.

blocks.q: counter = count_up(2); next(counter); next(counter); What does a third next(counter) do?
blocks.explain: The loop ended after 2, so the generator is finished and next() raises StopIteration.

salt = bytes(16)
stored = hashlib.scrypt(b'hunter2', salt=salt, n=2**14, r=8, p=1).hex()[:16]

blocks.note: A fixed salt keeps the output stable for this example; real code uses os.urandom(16) per user.

blocks.title: Running the script instead of sourcing it
blocks.text: Running bash set-mode.sh changes the copy inside a child shell, which then exits. Your shell still has no MODE, and the next command runs against the wrong settings.
